projects.title: Encrypted Sensitive Record Sync in Rust
projects.summary: This repo now persists encrypted sensitive records, stores provider tokens at rest with explicit key IDs, re-seals stale ciphertext in the background, and syncs a local HTTP-backed provider feed into Postgres.
projects.outcome: Shipped a bounded runtime proof surface for encrypted storage, application-level key rotation, persisted sensitive-access grants, background sync, and audited authorized-read decisions.
highlights: AES-256-GCM protects provider tokens and authorized record payloads at rest, and key-versioned ciphertext keeps mixed-key reads explicit during rotation.
Background token refresh and sync runs keep the proof surface current without widening the public claim surface.
The live lab shows guest-safe redaction, denied signed-in reads without grants, and audited authorized detail reads from the same stored data.

open_source_entries.name: statum
open_source_entries.summary: Representational correctness for workflow and protocol state, with typed rehydration and projection helpers for stored or append-only data.
highlights: Makes invalid, undesirable, or not-yet-validated states impossible to represent in ordinary code.
Uses #[state], #[machine], #[transition], and #[validators] to model legal phases and rebuild typed machines.
Exposes exact introspection, graph, and presentation surfaces for explainers, replay tooling, and generated docs.

badge.text: Legal and illegal states stop looking different only in comments

code_examples.label: Definitions
Call site

body.title: Legal edges become methods on the right machine type

features.text: LightSwitch<Off> and LightSwitch<On> are different types with different method surfaces.
The workflow shape moves into the type system instead of hiding in status enums, optional fields, and comments.

badge.text: State-specific data only exists when the machine is in that state

code_examples.label: State enum

body.title: Data-bearing states expose data only on the matching machine

features.text: Unit states validate with statum::Result<()>; data-bearing states return statum::Result<StateData>.
Review-only data stays off the draft and published machine types.

badge.text: Rows stay raw until validators prove a concrete state

code_examples.label: Validator
Rebuild

body.title: Stored data rebuilds into typed machines

features.text: Validator methods return Ok(()) or Ok(StateData) for the matching state, and InvalidState otherwise.
Projection helpers can fold append-only event streams before validator rebuilds when your source of truth is an event log.

open_source_entries.name: nestum
open_source_entries.summary: Proc-macro for nested enum paths that keeps the correct family boundary and removes constructor and match syntax tax.
highlights: Keeps nested enums when they are already the honest model of the domain.
Uses Event::Document::Created and nested! without flattening the enum model.
Supports focused nested! rewrites, #[nestum_scope], named-field constructors, and cross-module nesting.

badge.text: The outer enum stays a real envelope, but the surface reads like the tree

code_examples.label: Definitions
Construction
code_examples.code:
let inner: DocumentEvent::Enum = DocumentEvent::Created;
let event: Event::Enum = Event::Document::Created;

features.text: Event::Document is a namespace branch, not a completed Event value.
The generated surface keeps the family boundary instead of flattening the model.

badge.text: nested! rewrites patterns and named-field constructors where syntax gets noisy

body.title: Focused rewrites keep the nested vocabulary intact

features.text: nested! handles constructor and pattern positions without changing the enum model.
Named-field leaves still work without forcing a flatter API.

badge.text: Rewrite a whole function or impl body instead of wrapping every match

code_examples.label: Scope-level rewriting

body.title: Larger scopes and real projects stay coherent

features.text: #[nestum_scope] rewrites a whole function, method, impl, or inline module body.
The todo_api and ops_cli showcases keep Axum and Clap dispatch code aligned with the same nested command and event trees.

open_source_entries.name: modum
open_source_entries.summary: Workspace lint tool for Rust naming, import style, and public API paths that reports diagnostics without rewriting code.
highlights: Reports diagnostics instead of rewriting code, so teams can enforce policy without hidden edits.
Keeps namespace context visible at call sites instead of flattening it away.
Prefers strong semantic parents with short leaves like user::Repository over UserRepository.
Flags manual enum string helpers, ad hoc parse helpers, and other API-surface drift.

badge.text: Readable public paths become enforceable lint policy

code_examples.label: Noisy shape
Desired shape

body.title: A strong parent and short leaf become a linted standard

features.text: The tool flags redundant leaf context like user::UserRepository when the module path already carries the domain.
It keeps more descriptive leaves when the parent path is weak or technical.

badge.text: Flattened imports that hide useful context become diagnostics

body.title: Imports can preserve context instead of erasing it

features.text: Namespace-preserving modules can stay visible when the qualified call-site form adds net context.
Canonical parent-surface re-exports like pub use error::{Error, Result}; remain allowed.

badge.text: Run it like clippy, then tune it with workspace metadata

code_examples.label: CLI
code_examples.code:
cargo modum check --root .
cargo modum check --root . --mode warn --format json

body.title: Workspace policy lives in tooling, not review folklore

features.text: Use it in CI or editor integrations; the tool reports diagnostics but does not rewrite code.
JSON output, Cargo metadata, and namespace-preserving module rules let one workspace carry a consistent namespace policy.

work_cases.page_title: Current Proof | Encrypted Sensitive Record Sync
work_cases.title: Encrypted records, token lifecycle, and bounded background sync
work_cases.summary: A narrow secure-systems runtime slice: encrypted provider tokens and authorized payloads, deterministic stub sync by default, opt-in sandbox HTTPS, and a live lab that shows grants, denied reads, and audited access.

challenge.title: Challenge
items: The proof needed visible evidence for encrypted-at-rest storage, token handling, and explicit integration boundaries instead of only architecture notes.
The implementation had to stay bounded and honest about scope, without implying real healthcare or production provider operations.
The public surface needed one stored-record path that could show guest-safe redaction, denied reads, and audited authorized access.

implementation.title: Implementation
items: Added one sensitive-data bounded context across domain, app, infra, and HTTP without breaking the repo into extra crates.
Stored provider tokens and authorized record payloads with AES-256-GCM, while keeping only redacted labels and last-four evidence queryable in cleartext.

Built a two-mode provider boundary: deterministic local stub by default, plus an opt-in sandbox HTTP adapter with credential exchange, bounded retry/backoff, cursor-based sync, key-versioned ciphertext storage, persisted grants, and a live lab panel for denied-versus-allowed reads.

outcomes.title: Outcomes
items: The repo now backs secure-systems claims with a running encrypted-storage and background-sync slice instead of only narrative direction.
Reviewers can inspect token status, last sync state, redacted records, ciphertext evidence, denied reads, and audited authorized access in the live app.
The proof stays sanitized and bounded: deterministic stub mode for repeatable review, opt-in sandbox mode for real outbound HTTPS, and explicit trust boundaries.

work_cases.title: Automated fundraiser acknowledgments to remove high-volume backlog
work_cases.summary: This archived GoodUnited case study covers replacing a manual thank-you workflow with browser automation that increased throughput and consistency under operational pressure.

challenge.title: Challenge
items: Manual thank-you workflows were time-consuming, error-prone, and perpetually behind demand.
Teams depended on queue dashboards and manual triage but still accumulated backlog.
Large nonprofit clients generated very high monthly fundraiser volume, making manual scaling expensive.

implementation.title: Implementation
items: Built a Playwright + TypeScript automation worker to emulate the existing browser workflow end to end.
Encoded template selection and variable substitution logic to reduce operator variance and mistakes.
Scaled execution to 72 concurrent instances to keep pace with continuously arriving fundraiser pages.

outcomes.title: Outcomes
items: Delivered roughly 12x speed compared to a single manual operator for the same task shape.
Eliminated persistent backlog and reduced error rates in outbound fundraiser communication.
Faster response windows increased fundraiser engagement and improved downstream support effectiveness.

work_cases.title: Replaced delayed CSV workflows with realtime fundraiser + donation visibility
work_cases.summary: This archived fundraiser pipeline moved operations from delayed CSV snapshots to realtime creation and donation signals integrated with Meta APIs.

challenge.title: Challenge
items: Prior workflow depended on manually downloaded CSV files that were at least 48 hours delayed.
Teams could only see fundraisers after donations appeared, missing newly created but not-yet-donated pages.
The lag degraded outreach speed and reduced the ability to guide fundraisers effectively.

implementation.title: Implementation
items: Built an Express + Svelte + MongoDB app for event participants to create fundraisers in one click.
Integrated Meta APIs so fundraiser creation events were captured at source instead of inferred later.
Surfaced donation activity in realtime, enabling chat and success teams to operate with current context.

outcomes.title: Outcomes
items: Eliminated 48-hour baseline delay in fundraiser discovery and donation context.
Enabled operations across millions of users and tens of millions of donation data points.
Improved decision quality across sales, customer success, and analytics functions.

work_cases.title: Built a custom Substack publishing platform around a CMS event pipeline
work_cases.summary: This archived Rust publishing platform ingests Directus CMS events, processes them through queued workers, and executes automated publishing flows through a custom Substack integration.

challenge.title: Challenge
items: Editorial and publishing workflows needed reliable automation across CMS content lifecycle events.
Substack operations required custom integration logic because official API support was limited for needed flows.
The system had to preserve determinism and observability across asynchronous event processing.

implementation.title: Implementation
items: Built a custom Substack client/integration layer for publish-oriented automation paths.
Typed Directus webhook events by collection/operation and routed them into queue-backed processing.
Structured a 13-crate Rust workspace across libs, services, and tools to keep boundaries explicit.
Used Axum services and worker processing to run end-to-end automation chains from trigger to publish.

outcomes.title: Outcomes
items: Replaced manual handoff-heavy publishing work with deterministic event-driven automation.
Created a reusable platform foundation for additional CMS-triggered automation chains.
Established a clear hardening roadmap through architecture review of reliability and CI/security gaps.
